source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Israeli Hebrew has only five vowels and only a few sounds that English lacks. Written Hebrew usually leaves out the vowels, so you learn each word's sound by ear.
reading: CAPITALS mark the stressed syllable. Most words stress the last syllable (sha-LOM), but common ones don't (BO-ker, MA-yim, EY-fo).
kh is the throaty sound. It is never the k in "key".
Vowels are short and clean: a, e, i, o, u. Never a lazy "uh".

sounds.name: Khet / Khaf
sounds.how: Like the ch in Scottish "loch". Modern Israelis say ח and the soft כ (ך at the end of a word) the same way.

sounds.name: Resh
sounds.how: Made at the back of the throat, like a French r: a light gargle. The English r (with the tongue curled) is understood but marks you as a tourist.

sounds.name: Tsadi
sounds.how: ts as in "cats", even at the start of a word. A final צ is written ץ.

sounds.name: Ayin / Alef
sounds.how: In everyday Israeli speech both are silent, or at most a light catch. The vowel simply starts.

sounds.name: Bet / Vav
sounds.how: ב is b with a dot inside and v without one, but the dots are usually left out, so learn each word by ear. ו used as a consonant is v.

sounds.name: Pe
sounds.how: Same idea as ב: p with a dot, f without. A final פ is written ף and is always f.

sounds.name: Shin / Sin
sounds.how: Usually sh, but sometimes s. Again, the dot that tells them apart is usually left out.

tips_source: "How it's said" tips are written for Wayword (not part of the dataset): how an Israeli speaker says the phrase at normal speed, next to the careful pronunciation line.

tips.please: In quick everyday speech it often shrinks to three syllables: be-vak-SHA.
tips.coffee: בבקשה often shrinks in quick speech: ka-FE, be-vak-SHA.
tips.know_a_little: קצת is a single syllable, with k, t and s run together: a-NEE yo-DE-a ktsat.
tips.say_again: The h of להגיד is often light or dropped in everyday speech: ef-SHAR le-a-GEED et ze shuv.
tips.nice_meeting: The h of להכיר is often light or dropped: na-EEM le-a-KEER.
tips.love_languages: The h of אוהב is often light or dropped: a-NEE o-EV lil-MOD sa-FOT.
tips.like_talking: The h of אוהב is often light or dropped: a-NEE o-EV le-da-BER it-KHA.
